findings.highlight: Sakura is walking happily besides me.
findings.evidenceJa: 隣りには桜が嬉しそうに歩いている
findings.governingReading: Sakura is walking happily beside him
findings.explanation: “Besides me” means “in addition to me,” producing a basic preposition error in otherwise simple narration.

findings.highlight: I guess it has been a while since I went to school with you.
findings.evidenceJa: まあ、桜と一緒に登校するのは珍しいか
findings.governingReading: I suppose it is unusual for me to go to school together with Sakura
findings.explanation: A statement about the event being unusual becomes a claim specifically about elapsed time since the last occurrence.

findings.highlight: we’ll be walking together either way
findings.evidenceJa: 桜が嫌がっても一緒になる
findings.governingReading: we would end up together even if Sakura objected
findings.explanation: The teasing hypothetical that Sakura might dislike walking with him disappears, flattening Shirou’s oblivious response to her hopeful question.

findings.highlight: Not to speak ill of anyone
findings.evidenceJa: あんまり比べるのも悪だけど
findings.governingReading: it may be unfair to compare them too much
findings.explanation: Shirou’s scruple about comparing Sakura with her peers is recast as concern that praising her would insult them.

findings.highlight: you’re the best in your grade
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の腕は一年じゃダントツだぞ
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s skill is far and away the best among the first-years
findings.explanation: The emphatic gap between Sakura and the other first-years is reduced to a bare ranking.

findings.highlight: My thoughts trail off if I let my guard down
findings.evidenceJa: 気を緩めると邪念が入る
findings.governingReading: distracting or impure thoughts intrude when she relaxes
findings.explanation: Intruding distractions become thoughts fading away, changing the mechanism Sakura says disrupts her shooting.

findings.highlight: unless I push myself to train a little every day
findings.evidenceJa: 毎日ピッシリやってないと
findings.governingReading: unless she trains strictly and without fail every day
findings.explanation: “A little every day” weakens Sakura’s severe account of the discipline she believes she requires.

findings.highlight: who am I to disagree?
findings.evidenceJa: 口を出す問題でもないか
findings.governingReading: it is not a matter for Shirou to interfere in
findings.explanation: A decision not to meddle becomes lack of standing to disagree, changing Shirou’s relation to Sakura’s judgment.

findings.highlight: My class is on the third floor, and hers is on the fourth.
findings.evidenceJa: 二年は三階、一年である桜の教室は四階である
findings.governingReading: the second-year rooms are on the third floor, while first-year Sakura’s classroom is on the fourth
findings.explanation: A general school layout is narrowed into the locations of only Shirou’s and Sakura’s individual classes.

findings.highlight: I’m not full anymore.
findings.evidenceJa: もうとっくにお腹八分目になってますから
findings.governingReading: she is already back down to being comfortably, roughly eighty-percent full
findings.explanation: Sakura’s cheerful claim that she remains comfortably full is reversed into no longer being full at all.

findings.highlight: there are more people absent
findings.evidenceJa: 他にも何人かの病欠者がいた
findings.governingReading: several other pupils are absent due to illness
findings.explanation: The illness shared by the additional absentees disappears, weakening the link to the continuing coma cases.

findings.highlight: the number of absentees shouldn’t get any higher, at least
findings.evidenceJa: 欠席者はこれ以上増える事はない
findings.governingReading: the number of absentees will not increase any further
findings.explanation: Shirou’s categorical but limited-perspective assurance is softened into a tentative expectation.

findings.highlight: There should be no more unexplained comas.
findings.evidenceJa: 原因不明の昏睡事件はもう起きないのだ
findings.governingReading: the unexplained coma incidents will happen no more
findings.explanation: A second categorical conclusion by Shirou is again weakened into probability, dulling the confidence Rin will soon challenge.

findings.highlight: until I know what kind of people they are
findings.evidenceJa: 残る二人がどんなマスターなのか判らない
findings.governingReading: until he knows what kind of Masters the remaining two are
findings.explanation: The unknown pair’s relevant capacity as Masters is generalized into their personalities as people.

findings.highlight: I bump into Tohsaka the instant I go out into the hallway.
findings.evidenceJa: 不意打ちぎみに遠坂と顔を合わせてしまった
findings.governingReading: he unexpectedly comes face-to-face with Rin, almost as if caught by surprise
findings.explanation: The ambush-like quality of the sudden encounter disappears.

findings.highlight: Isn’t that a rude thing to say?
findings.evidenceJa: 人の顔を見るなり失礼なんじゃない？
findings.governingReading: isn’t that rude, the instant you see my face?
findings.explanation: Rin’s mock complaint specifically targets Shirou’s immediate reaction to seeing her; the English reduces it to generic rudeness.

findings.highlight: the same goes for you, you were surprised too
findings.evidenceJa: 今の台詞はそっくりそのまま返してやる
findings.governingReading: I’ll return those exact words to you
findings.explanation: The pointed formulation that Rin’s own line applies word-for-word to her is replaced by a loose paraphrase.

findings.highlight: Did Tohsaka feel responsible because she told me about it?
findings.evidenceJa: あんなコトぐらいで責任を感じてたってのか？
findings.governingReading: could she have felt responsible over something as minor as that?
findings.explanation: Shirou’s surprised minimization of the reason for Rin’s guilt disappears.

findings.highlight: You’re absolutely certain that you defeated Caster?
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方、本当にキャスターを倒したの？
findings.governingReading: did you really defeat Caster?
findings.explanation: Rin asks whether the event actually occurred; the English shifts her test toward Shirou’s subjective confidence.

findings.highlight: …Caster’s Master is
findings.evidenceJa: ……キャスターのマスターだって、もう
findings.governingReading: and Caster’s Master was already…
findings.explanation: The English leaves a present-tense copula dangling before narration reveals the Master was already dead, making the interrupted clarification grammatically malformed.
